_comment: An hourly full suite CANCELLED WITHOUT EVER GETTING A RUNNER — the shape that makes duration
useless as a timeout test, and the reason `run_job_dispatched` exists.
`runner_name` is null and there are no step timings, because nothing ran. But GitHub still stamps
`started_at = created_at` and `completed_at` at the moment of cancellation, so the arithmetic
yields 86 MINUTES — comfortably past `timeout-minutes: 45`, and indistinguishable by size from a
The numbers are real: run 33989185479 on 2026-09-05 was created 20:08:03 and its job did not
start until 21:34:21 — 86 minutes of queue on a saturated seat. That run DID eventually dispatch
and time out; this fixture is the counterfactual in which it had been cancelled while waiting,
which is exactly what happened to the 21:06 run that concluded `cancelled` with no hourly job
Without the dispatch guard this payload substitutes a TIMED_OUT_CANCEL sentinel and BLOCKS THE
MERGE QUEUE on a suite that never executed. A false block is the expensive direction and nothing
downstream can tell it from a real one.
